privacy_commitment_text: Class of Happiness is committed to protecting the privacy of all users, especially children. We comply with GDPR (EU/UK) and follow COPPA principles for child safety. We never sell, rent, or share personal data with advertisers or third parties.
privacy_data_collect_text:
• Teachers and Parents: Email address, name, app usage data
• Students: First name, avatar, emotion check-ins, strategy choices
• Technical: Session tokens, language preference, anonymised error logs
• We do NOT collect location data, contacts, or payment card details
privacy_data_use_text: Data is used only to operate the app, supporting emotional awareness for students, teachers, and families. We use anonymised data to fix bugs and improve features. We never use data for advertising or sell it to any third party.
privacy_full_policy_text: Our full privacy policy is available at classofhappiness.com/privacy-policy.html
privacy_retention_text: Student check-in data is retained for up to 12 months. Account data is deleted within 30 days of account closure. All data is transmitted over encrypted HTTPS connections. Passwords are never stored in plain text.
privacy_rights_text: You have the right to access, correct, delete, or export your data at any time. Parents may request review or deletion of their child's data. Contact us at {email}. We respond within 30 days.
privacy_security_text: We use industry-standard encryption and security measures to protect your data. All data is transmitted securely and stored on protected servers.
privacy_student_safety_text:
• We never advertise to students
• Students do not create independent accounts
• Student data is identified by first name and avatar only
• Student check-in data is visible only to their teacher and linked parent
• No location data, contacts, or device identifiers are collected from students
privacy_third_party_text: We use Supabase (database), Railway (hosting), Stripe (payments), and Expo (push notifications). All providers are contractually required to process data only as instructed and in compliance with data protection law.

strat_body_checkin_desc: Ask "Where do you feel this in your body?" Noticing physical sensations interrupts the spiral and increases interoceptive awareness.
strat_box_breathing_desc: Breathe in 4, hold 4, out 4, hold 4. Do it WITH your child — modelling is more powerful than instruction.
strat_calm_problem_desc: When things are calm, solve problems together: "What could we do differently next time?" Green zone is ideal for collaborative planning.
strat_cold_water_desc: Splash cold water on the face or hold a cold drink. This activates the dive reflex, rapidly reducing heart rate.
strat_comfort_desc: Encourage connection with a pet, soft toy or blanket. Physical comfort activates the parasympathetic nervous system.
strat_creative_desc: Draw, build, cook or make something with no goal in mind. Open-ended play activates curiosity and strengthens connection.
strat_dance_desc: Put on a favourite upbeat song and move together. Music + movement + laughter = powerful social bonding.
strat_gratitude_desc: Each family member shares one thing they appreciated today. Builds positive neural pathways and strengthens family cohesion over time.
strat_journal_desc: Offer a notebook to write or draw feelings. Externalising emotions reduces intensity and builds long-term emotional literacy.
strat_lowered_desc: Explicitly say "Today we can take it easy." Removing performance pressure allows natural energy to return without shame.
strat_movement_desc: Suggest a 5-minute walk outside. Even slow movement increases serotonin and dopamine. Invite — never force.
strat_name_it_desc: Gently name what you see: "You seem really low today." Labelling emotions reduces amygdala activation by up to 50%.
strat_no_teaching_desc: Wait until the red zone passes before discussing what happened. The reasoning brain goes offline during high arousal.
strat_one_on_one_desc: 10-15 minutes of undivided attention where your child leads. Non-negotiable — significantly reduces attention-seeking behaviour.
strat_playful_desc: For younger children — a funny face or ridiculous sound can work. Laughter physically downregulates the stress response.
strat_reconnect_desc: After the storm, reconnect with warmth first: a hug, eye contact, soft voice. Only then address behaviour — calmly.
strat_regulate_desc: Your nervous system regulates theirs. Take one slow breath before responding. Children co-regulate through adult calm — not words.
strat_repair_desc: If you lost your cool, model repair: "I'm sorry I raised my voice. Let's try again." Repair is more powerful than perfection.
strat_safe_space_desc: Guide your child to a quiet corner WITH you nearby. Isolation increases shame; proximity while calm reduces it.
strat_side_by_side_desc: Sit quietly next to your child without expectation. No screens, no fixing — just presence. Research shows co-regulation starts with felt safety.
strat_space_desc: Say "I'll give you 5 minutes and come back to check on you." Respects autonomy while maintaining warm connection.
strat_strength_desc: Point out a specific strength: "I noticed how patient you were today." Specific praise builds a secure self-concept.
strat_validate_desc: Before solving, say "That makes sense you'd feel that way." Validation reduces emotional intensity within 90 seconds.
strat_warm_drink_desc: Make a warm drink together. The act of preparing something nourishing activates the caregiving system and signals safety.
